FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 16 February 1990, after the draft finalized by the Ear, Nose and Throat Surgery Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Division Council. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).' The number of significant places retained in the roun&bff value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ENT SURGERY INSTRUMENTS-LARYNGEAL FORCEPS, OVAL CUP-SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE
1.1 This standard

4.3 Joint The joint shall be as specified in IS 3642 ( Part 1 ) : 1990. The joint shall be rivetted. 4.4 Finger Loops The finger loops shall conform 3642 ( Part 1 ) : 1990. 5 HEAT TREATMENT 5.1 The component parts of the forceps shall he heat treated under suitable conditions to give a hardness of 540 to 640 HV. 5.2 Mating surface of the same instrument, such as, opposite jaws, blades and shanks shall not vary in hardness by more than 40 HV. 6 WORKMANSHIP 6.1 The forceps shall have a joint which moves smoothly and shall neither be too loose nor too tight. 6.2 It shall be possible to close and reopen the instrument easily with two fingers without stiffness and there shall be no play at the joint. 6.3 The maximum opening of the upper jaw shall correspond to the maximum opening of the finger loop, that is, when the finger loops are open to their maximum position, the upper jaw shall not move further to its maximum opening. 6.4 The jaws shall open and close fully and freely without any stiffness. The jaws shall register accurately and shall close completely without any gap when the forceps are closed. 6.5 The upper jaw shall move freely and smoothly. 6.6 All the edges shall be rounded unless specified otherwise,. and the edges of the cups shall be sharp. 7 SURFACE CONDITION 7.1 General All surfaces shall be free from pores, cracks, seams, burs, flaws, crevices and grinding marks. The instrument shall be supplied free from residual scale, acid, grease and grinding and pohshing materials. 7.2 Surface Finish The instrument shall have-satin finish. 1 to Size 1 of IS

covers dimensional and other requirements for oval cup laryngeal forceps used in ENT surgery. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The following Indian Standards adjuncts to this standard :

3 MATERIAL 3.1 The components of forceps shall be made of stainless steel conforming to Designation 3OCr13 of IS 6603 : 1972. 4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 4.1 The shape and dimensions shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 4.2 Tolerances 4.2.1 The tolerances on linear dimensions shall be as follows: a) f 0'05 mm on dimensions up to 2'0 mm, b) rt 0'1 mm on dimensions above 2'0 mm and up to 5'0 mm, c) f 0'2 mm on dimensions above 5'0 mm and up to 20'0 mm, d) f 0'5 mm on dimensions above 20.0 mm and up to 50'0 mm, e) -+ 1'0 mm on dimensions ahove 50'0 mm and up to 100'0 mm, and f) f 2'0 mm on dimensions above 100'0 mm. 4.2.2 Tolerances on angular dimensions shall be as follows: a) f 1" for angles up to lo", and b) f 2" for angles greater than 10". 4.2.3 The two halves of the instruments shall, however, nodiffer at any dimension, and shall match with each other perfectly.

IS 12911 : 1990 7.3 Passivation and Fidal Treatment The instrument shall be treated by a suitable passivation process, for example, by electroplating or by treatment with 10 percent ( V/V) nitric acid solution for not less than 30 minutes at a temperature of not less than 10�C and not exceeding 60�C. The instrument shall then be rinsed in water and dried in hot air.
NOTE -If the joint is lubricated, then the lubricant rhall be non-corrosive and suitable for medical application according to Indian Pharmacopoea. 8

8.3.1.3 Procedure Immerse the instrument in the test solution contained in the beaker at room temperature for 6 minutes. Remove the instrument and wash it with distilled water or water of equivalent quality, or wipe it with wet cotton wool. Examine the instrument for evidence of copper deposits. 8.3.2 Boiling Water Test
8.3.2.1 Reagent

Distilled or de-ionized water. 8.3.2.2 Apparatus Glass or ceramic beaker or suitable resistant stainless steel vessel. 8.3.2.3 Preparation of sample Scrub the instrument using soap and warm water, rinse thoroughly in water ( 8.3.2.1 ) and dry. 8.3.2.4 Procedure Immerse the instrument in boiling water ( 8.3.2.1) in the beaker or vessel for at least 30 minutes. Subsequently, allow the instrument to cool for at least 1 hour in the water used for the test. Then remove the instrument from water and leave it exposed to the air for 2 hours. Rub the instrument vigorously with a dry cloth and examine it for the presence of blemishes. 9 MARKING 9.1 Marking on the Instrnment The instrument shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the indication of the source of manufacture the letter `0' or the words `Stainless Steel' and the country of manufacture. 9.2 Marking on Cartons The cartons or packages containing the forceps shall bear markings as on the instrument. In addition, the carton -or the box shall also be marked with the name of the instrument and any other information that is required by the purchaser or the laws in force. 10 PACKING 10.1 Each instrument shall individually be either put in a polyethylene bag or wrapped in wax paper. Each instrument shall then be packed in carton as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer or in accordance with the current trade practices. corrosion-

TESTS

8.1 Hardness The forceps shall be tested for hardness as specified in 5.1 in accordance with IS 1501. 8.2 Flexibility The jaws of the forceps shall be made to bite a double layer of wet blotting paper. The jaws shall have clear impression of complete sharp edge on the blotting paper. The jaws of the forceps shall also be made to bite a -piece of soft rubber sheet about 1 mm thick and the finger loops closed as fully as possible [ applying a force of about 1 Newton ( I kgf approx ) 1. The cutting edges shall be examined under a magnification of 10x along the plane of the cutting edges for feathers, nicks, waviness, etc; on release, the forceps shall not show any sign of damage or the upper jaw shall not become loose at its hinges. 8.3 Corrosion Resistance The forceps shall be tested for resistance against corrosion both by copper sulphate test and boiling water test as given in 8.3.1 and 8.3.2. The forceDs shall not show any _ sign - of corrosion after eac6 test. 8.3.1 Copper Sulphate Test
